title: Drive-style sharing: folders shared with users and nested groups, inherited down the folder tree
issue: Access = a share on the document's folder or any ancestor folder, granted to the user or to any group the user belongs to directly or through nested groups. A policy has to walk two graphs (folder ancestors and group parents) with recursive CTEs, per row, or call a security definer function that expands them, once per statement, or maintain closure tables on every write.
symptom: Measured at 50k documents: naive_rls (recursive ancestor walk per document) takes ~280 ms for a full count against 0.1-2 ms for every other variant, and is 2-30x slower on recent/search; recursive_fn_rls and closure-table best_practice_rls are within ~2x of the baseline because the folder set is only 1000 folders.

scale.meaning: number of documents; folders = scale/50 (min 1000, 4-ary tree, 50 documents per folder), 364 groups (3-ary tree, 6 levels, fixed), scale/100 users (min 100) in 2 groups each, ~700 shares. 10x = 500k documents, 10k folders (folder_closure ~70k rows), 5k users; OpenFGA tuples = folders + groups + memberships + shares (~2k at default, ~25k at 10x), never per document.

subjects.name: direct
subjects.note: one direct share on folder 100 (a level-4 folder, ~2% of the tree), in no group

subjects.name: deep_group
subjects.note: member of one leaf group, 6 levels below the root group; shares on that group and on 4 of its ancestor groups (~10% of the tree)

subjects.name: big_group
subjects.note: member of group 3 which owns folder 2: a quarter of the folder tree and of the documents
